quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black symbols warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be consistently checked by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be consistently checked by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Riders should turn their head to check for traffic before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: White signs with red and black markings show traffic laws. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has suddenly gone flat is that:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
A discharge of air can be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of the motorcycle will jerk or sway side to side. If you feel this movement, stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: Which factor does not play a major role in affecting your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Age does not have a major effect on BAC.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black symbols warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic ahead is merging.

questions.question: During normal turns:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean in the same direction.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean in the same direction.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, the rider and motorcycle should lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, the motorcycle leans while the rider stays more upright to balance.

questions.question: If you must transport a load, it should be:

options.text: Carried on the gas tank in front of you.
Piled up against a sissy bar or frame on the back of the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carried over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on a motorcycle.

questions.question: Increase your following distance if:
questions.correctAnswerText: It is raining.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop, when you can't see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy and vehicles may cut in front of you.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull onto the shoulder and wait for it to stop raining.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the center of the lane when rain starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: How should passengers hold on?

options.text: Hold the rider's hips, waist, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to hold your hips, waist, or belt firmly. They can also hold any secure handholds on the motorcycle.

questions.question: How should a rider safely turn a motorcycle?

options.text: Lean in the direction of the turn.
Slow down while in the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Lean in the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: When should you wear hearing protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: On every ride.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection every time you ride to prevent hearing damage.

questions.question: How should your arms be positioned on a motorcycle?

options.text: Bent a lot at the elbow when reaching the handlebars.
Slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
Fully extended when reaching the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you press the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms support your weight.
Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms can control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit in a way that lets your arms control the motorcycle. Do not position yourself so your arms have to support your body weight.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What should be your top concern when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.correctAnswerText: Protection.
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important factor when choosing a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: Where should you ride when passing parked vehicles on your right with no oncoming traffic?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to avoid hazards like opening car doors or pedestrians stepping out. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: What color clothing should you wear when riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be more visible while riding, even during the day. Reflective materials also help increase your visibility.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: How should you brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a potential problem?

options.text: The road surface is about to change
Road conditions that do not change as you get closer

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions that do not change as you get closer
questions.explanation: Look ahead for possible problems on the road. Make a plan to stay safe from them.

questions.question: Before riding, check the throttle. It should:

options.text: Stay in place when you let go
Feel loose when you let go
Snap back when you let go

questions.correctAnswerText: Snap back when you let go
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your clutch and throttle. The throttle should snap back to its resting position when released. The clutch should feel firm and smooth.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Mirrors show everything you need to see
Mirrors cannot show your blind spots
You should only use mirrors when parking

questions.correctAnswerText: Mirrors cannot show your blind spots
questions.explanation: Like all vehicles, motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: You have less grip for braking when:
questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle is leaning
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during a turn, there is less grip available for braking. You can still use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: Your position in the lane should:

options.text: Help you blend in with other traffic
Give you a way to escape if danger appears
Encourage other drivers to share your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a way to escape if danger appears
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to help you see and be seen. Avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if a problem occurs.

questions.question: Use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch when:

options.text: The throttle is stuck and will not move
You start to lose control on a curve

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and will not move
questions.explanation: If your throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, immediately use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch. This removes power from the back wheel so you can safely stop.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes or boots that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Bad braking technique:

options.text: Is a major cause of motorcycle crashes
Is not important since motorcycles have two brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of motorcycle crashes
questions.explanation: Poor braking technique causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning the right way to brake is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: All motorcycles must have:

options.text: A rearview mirror on the left handlebar
A rearview mirror on the right handlebar
A rearview mirror only if the rider is under 21

questions.correctAnswerText: A rearview mirror on the left handlebar
questions.explanation: Tennessee law requires all motorcycles to have a rearview mirror mounted on the left handlebar in an upright position.
